 SK hynix Stocks Climb 5.36% as Foreign Investors Pile Back Into AI Memory
 Less than 1 min read 000660 SK hynix (HXSCL) shares climbed 5.36%, or 65,000 won, to 1,277,000 won at the Seoul regular-session close on Wednesday, November 11, outpacing the Kospi's 2.60% gain. Foreign investors net bought 449.1 billion won on the day, focusing on SK hynix and Samsung. 
 SK hynix's third quarter delivered revenue of 104.6 trillion won, up 328% year over year, and operating profit of 83.3 trillion won, an 80% margin. Long-term agreements with 14 major customers cover more than half of 20272028 capacity, and management expects demand to exceed supply through 2030. The Korea Times reported that HBM and other DRAM are sold out through 2029, alongside a roughly 100 trillion won shareholder return plan for 2026. 
 The third-quarter dividend of 20,000 won per share, including a 10,000 won special payout, equals about 1.6% of Wednesday's closing price for a single quarter. Contracted capacity lowers volume risk, but pricing resets inside those agreements remain the swing factor. GuruFocus gives SK hynix's U.S. depositary line a GF Score of 98/100, with Profitability Rank 10/10, Financial Strength 9/10, Momentum Rank 9/10 and GF Value Rank 6/10. The next test is HBM4 overtaking HBM3E in fourth-quarter shipments and revenue.
